articles.title: Samsung’s 5K monitor has good gaming chops and a great price
articles.summary: There are quite a few 5K monitors out there. Many of them are designed to appeal to Mac users who are looking for cheaper Studio Display alternatives without giving up the pixel-dense 218ppi screen. However, if you’re interested in hearing about one with…
articles.content: There are quite a few 5K monitors out there. Many of them are designed to appeal to Mac users who are looking for cheaper Studio Display alternatives without giving up the pixel-dense 218ppi screen. However, if you’re interested in hearing about one with gaming chops, Samsung’s 27-inch Odyssey G80HF seems like one of the best monitors out there to satisfy your niche, but respectable desires. Currently, you can grab this model for $599.99 at Amazon and B&H Photo , which beats its best price by $100. Samsung 27-inch Odyssey G8 5K monitor Where to Buy: $949.99 $599.99 at Amazon $949.99 $599.9 at B&H Photo The G80HF supports two display modes with its Fast IPS panel: 5K at up to 180Hz refresh rate, or 1440p with up to a 360Hz refresh rate. Samsung touts Nvidia G-Sync compatibility as well as AMD FreeSync Premium to ensure the monitor’s refresh rate remains in lockstep with your GPU’s frame rate output. The monitor features a DisplayPort 2.1 port (just one, and Samsung doesn’t advertise its bandwidth), two HDMI 2.1 ports, and a USB hub for charging or connecting two USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 accessories. As a gamer, one of my favorite features here is the one-millisecond response time. That’s a very common spec among gaming monitors — even in ones that cost hundreds less — but it’s a bit of a rare spec in a 5K monitor at this price. I tested KTC’s sub-$500 model last year , and gaming on it was a pretty atrocious experience despite having what it claimed to be gaming-ready capabilities. For $200 more ($799.99), LG’s 27-inch UltraGear evo 5K Mini LED monitor delivers slightly better specs. It has more dimming zones for a more accurate picture, it can get brighter, and it supports USB-C video input with 90W power delivery output to charge your device as you use it. Its dual mode refresh rates aren’t as high as Samsung’s (165Hz / 330Hz), but I don’t really see that as much of a downside. Other great deals happening now For those who haven’t yet placed a preorder for Grand Theft Auto VI , which comes out in less than a month, you can do so while saving $10 on a gaming gift card at Best Buy. The retailer is letting customers build a bundle of select games and gift cards. You can, for example, add GTA VI and a gift card will be $10 off its advertised price at checkout. It’s a small, but welcome way to save a little cash. The bundle includes other current and upcoming blockbusters, like Gears of War: E-Day , Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , and more. The excellent remake of Demon’s Souls by the shuttered PlayStation studio , Bluepoint Games, is down to just $13.49 in digital format on the PlayStation Store. What’s more, it’s for the digital deluxe edition (originally $89.99), which includes in-game cosmetics, a consumable that grants you a bunch of souls for in-game upgrades, and the soundtrack. The sale lasts through November 4th on the West Coast, or until 2:59AM ET on November 5th on the East Coast. The remake doesn’t mess with the formula of FromSoftware’s PS3 cult classic (it has stages instead of being an open-world like its spiritual successor, Dark Souls ), but gives it some brilliant visuals and fast loading times. It’s definitely worth a try if you’re into other Soulslike games that reward (and test) your patience. Read our review of the game . If you need a multi-port wall charger to quickly charge a bunch of USB-C devices, Ugreen’s Nexode Pro is down to $59.99 at Amazon and Ugreen , a $30 discount off the usual cost. The price was $10 lower during June’s Prime Day, but this is still a nice value. Despite the charger advertising 160W charging passthrough, its USB-C ports labeled C1 and C2 each top out at 140W when just one device is plugged into the charger. The power of each port (four USB-C, one USB-A) varies depending on how many gadgets are plugged in, up to 160W total. The charger has folding prongs and a display that can rotate depending on how it’s plugged in.

articles.summary: Water and fresh food running out in Taiz as fighting intensifies and Houthi advance cuts off most supply routes The humanitarian crisis in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz is becoming unmanageable as the city runs out of water, fuel and fresh food, Oxfam aid…

articles.content: Two critical vulnerabilities have been identified with PHP, a programming language which is widely used across the internet.
articles.aiArticle:
Operators of online platforms face a stark ultimatum from cybersecurity authorities: apply urgent software patches or take their domains offline immediately. According to BBC News, the directive comes in response to **two critical vulnerabilities** discovered within **PHP**, a foundational programming language that powers a massive share of web infrastructure globally. 

## The Core Technical Flaws

The unfolding situation stems directly from severe security gaps found inside the widely deployed language. While the exact mechanics of the flaws remain restricted to technical advisories, the potential fallout is severe enough to warrant extraordinary intervention from defensive agencies. Website administrators are being told that hesitation could leave their systems exposed to malicious actors capable of exploiting the unpatched code.

As development teams scramble to deploy fixes, the pressure highlights how fragile foundational web architecture can be when sudden flaws emerge. This incident shares similarities with other recent infrastructure pressures, such as how [a critical PHP vulnerability may take websites down today](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/a-critical-php-vulnerability-may-take-websites-down-today) and disrupt routine digital operations.

## Why This Matters

PHP has served as a backbone for web development for decades, supporting everything from small blogs to massive enterprise portals. When a foundational technology like this develops widespread security flaws, the stakes immediately scale to cover millions of interconnected systems. For everyday users and business owners alike, an unpatched vulnerability means potential data breaches, unauthorized server access, or total site outages that can cripple online commerce. 

This environment compounds existing digital pressures, forcing smaller firms to contend with security demands that often outpace their technical resources. In an era where companies must already navigate complex digital demands—much like how [Blackwall quadruples valuation to $2.2B as websites wrangle an increasingly crowded internet](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/blackwall-quadruples-valuation-to-b-as-websites-wrangle-an-increasingly-crowded-internet)—infrastructure stability remains a constant baseline requirement for survival.

## What to Watch

Observers should monitor how quickly hosting providers and independent webmasters can push updates across their networks before malicious exploitation scales. Key indicators of success will include official patching rates reported by cybersecurity watchdogs and whether any widespread outages materialize over the coming operational cycle.

French President **Emmanuel Macron** has forcefully condemned external commentary regarding ongoing unrest within his country, labeling outside remarks from foreign leaders as both "unacceptable" and "stupid," according to World news | The Guardian. Speaking out against what he termed a clear attempt to manipulate facts, Macron expressed deep frustration with the widespread distortion of information surrounding the domestic protests unfolding in France.

The French leader's sharp rebuke arrives as international attention remains heavily fractured across multiple concurrent geopolitical flashpoints. While European capitals grapple with internal civil demonstrations and the public fallout from foreign leaders weighing in, diplomatic channels elsewhere are actively shifting. Notably, these tensions run parallel to high-level diplomatic maneuvers involving the United States and Russia, which include recent discussions in St Petersburg as well as developments concerning detained American citizens. For more details on these concurrent diplomatic tracks, readers can review our coverage on how the [US citizen Stephen Hubbard freed by Russia as Trump envoy meets Putin](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/us-citizen-stephen-hubbard-freed-by-russia-as-trust-envoy-meets-putin).

## Diplomatic Friction and Domestic Unrest

According to the report from The Guardian, the French president's frustration centers squarely on the visible manipulation of narrative and facts by figures outside France. By characterizing foreign commentary on French street protests as careless and unjustifiable, Macron is pushing back against external actors who seek to weaponize domestic European instability for their own strategic messaging. This friction underscores the delicate nature of cross-border relations within the West, where public statements from allied nations can rapidly inflame local political sensitivities.

Historically, European nations have navigated complex internal protests while attempting to maintain a unified diplomatic front against external pressures. However, the modern information environment allows foreign leaders to instantly amplify fringe narratives, complicating how local governments manage domestic civil disobedience.

## Why This Matters

This public rebuke highlights the growing vulnerability of democratic states to information warfare and cross-border political interference during domestic crises. When foreign leaders openly critique or mischaracterize internal security events, it deepens polarization, undermines institutional trust, and complicates bilateral alliances. For everyday citizens and policymakers alike, the stakes involve the integrity of national sovereignty and the challenge of maintaining factual consensus when foreign actors actively promote distorted accounts of local unrest.

## What to Watch

Observers will monitor whether European capitals issue formal diplomatic reprimands or if bilateral talks between France and the involved nations experience lingering chill effects. Future public appearances by Macron will also reveal if Paris intends to escalate its pushback against foreign commentators exploiting domestic demonstrations.

articles.content: The 74-year-old former teacher has been released without any "swap" required, Trump says.
articles.aiArticle:
An American national imprisoned by Moscow has regained his freedom, returning home without the administration needing to orchestrate a formal prisoner exchange, according to statements made by Donald Trump. 

The individual at the center of the diplomatic development is **Stephen Hubbard**, a **74-year-old** former teacher whose detention previously strained relations between Washington and the Kremlin. BBC News reported that the release materialized concurrently with high-level diplomatic maneuvers, as a special envoy dispatched by Trump held direct discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

## Diplomatic Breakthrough Without Prisoner Swaps

While numerous high-profile releases involving American citizens detained abroad historically require complex bilateral trades—often involving Russian nationals held in Western facilities—this particular instance bucked the trend. According to Trump, the elderly educator was freed unconditionally, with no reciprocal prisoner swap demanded by Moscow. The breakthrough occurred as political channels opened up directly between the White House envoy and the Russian leadership, yielding immediate humanitarian results. For readers following these shifts in international diplomacy, our ongoing coverage includes analysis on the [former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine on Trump's turn toward Russia](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/former-u-s-ambassador-to-ukraine-on-trump-s-turn-toward-russia), detailing how evolving political strategies impact foreign policy outcomes.

## Broader Context and Background

The diplomatic maneuvering surrounding Hubbard's release highlights the complex web of negotiations that occasionally runs parallel to ongoing geopolitical conflicts. Historically, the arrest and imprisonment of foreign nationals have served as diplomatic leverage between adversarial nations, making unconditioned releases a notable departure from standard diplomatic friction. This dynamic has frequently drawn intense scrutiny from international allies monitoring Washington's bilateral outreach. Additional regional updates and reactions from European figures regarding shifting diplomatic postures can be reviewed in our report on how [Macron blasts ‘unacceptable’ and ‘stupid’ commentary on protests from other leaders – Europe live](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/macron-blasts-unacceptable-and-stupid-commentary-on-protests-from-other-leaders-europe).

## Why This Matters

For Washington, securing a release without conceding reciprocal demands demonstrates the potential efficacy of direct personal diplomacy, though critics often worry about the long-term precedent such unilateral engagements set. For the families of other Americans still held abroad, such developments offer both renewed hope and difficult questions about which cases receive priority attention from high-level envoys.

## What to Watch

The early passage of play featured a fierce bowling spell from **Kagiso Rabada**. The report states that the South African fast bowler operated at serious pace, maintaining immense pressure on the crease despite questions over radar readings. At the non-striker and striker ends, **Travis Head** had advanced to **14** runs while **Marnus Labuschagne** contributed **6**, weathering the storm as the Proteas attack probed for a third scalp.

St George’s Park has a rich history of hosting fiercely contested matches between these two cricketing powerhouses, often yielding dramatic momentum shifts in red-ball encounters. Following earlier disruptions in the series—such as when a wet outfield caused delays on day two, as detailed in our coverage of the [South Africa v Australia wet outfield second men's cricket Test day two delays](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/south-africa-v-australia-wet-outfield-causing-delays-in-second-men-s)—both sides are eager to maximize every available hour of play. The ongoing contest follows tactical lessons from earlier fixtures, including how Australia's pace attack has historically exposed batting vulnerabilities, a dynamic explored further in our report on how [Boland exposed South Africa's frailties to give Robinson a blueprint](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/boland-exposes-south-africa-s-frailties-to-give-robinson-blueprint).

## Why This Matters

Test matches between South Africa and Australia carry immense weight in the international red-ball arena, often shaping the upper echelons of the sport's rankings and psychological dominance. For the players, executing under the intense pressure of a hostile away crowd or defending home turf defines careers, while supporters experience high-stakes drama that tests the endurance of traditional five-day cricket. articles.summary: Michael 'Venom' Page says MMA fighters need to form a union and "move as one" if they want to secure better pay in the sport.
articles.content: Michael 'Venom' Page says MMA fighters need to form a union and "move as one" if they want to secure better pay in the sport.
articles.aiArticle:
Mixed martial arts athletes must unite and organize collectively if they ever hope to secure fairer compensation, according to veteran fighter **Michael 'Venom' Page**. Speaking on the financial state of the sport, the prominent competitor argued that individual athletes lack the leverage needed to negotiate better financial terms on their own.

## The Push for Collective Bargaining

Athletes in the upper echelons of combat sports often command substantial purses, but the broader roster of competitors frequently struggles with compensation structures. According to **BBC Sport**, Page emphasized that real change in remuneration will only happen when competitors stop acting as isolated agents and begin to "move as one." By establishing a formal union, fighters could pool their bargaining power to challenge existing promotional pay models, much like labor organizations do in other professional industries. Similar labor disputes frequently arise across various sectors when employees push back against corporate policies, mirroring the [Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/union-attacks-natwest-plans-to-get-workers-back-to-the-office) situation where workers rallied against corporate mandates.

## Broader Industry Stakes

This call for collective organization highlights a long-standing debate within combat sports regarding revenue sharing between promoters and athletes. Unlike major team sports governed by strict collective bargaining agreements, mixed martial arts has historically relied on individual contracts that critics argue heavily favor large promotional companies. If fighters successfully organize, it could fundamentally reshape the economics of the sport, shifting financial security and healthcare benefits toward the competitors who absorb the physical risks.

Industry observers will be monitoring whether Page's comments gain traction among active competitors, or if the fragmented nature of mixed martial arts will continue to hinder large-scale organizing efforts.

Sources: [BBC Sport](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/mixed-martial-arts/articles/cqe9ldzp9n73o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

articles.title: Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs
articles.summary: Kashim Chowdhury was contracted for 183 hours a week, more than the number of hours in seven days.
articles.content: Kashim Chowdhury was contracted for 183 hours a week, more than the number of hours in seven days.
articles.aiArticle:
A government official in public administration has acknowledged committing errors while simultaneously managing **five** different public sector positions, an arrangement that demanded an impossible workload of **183 hours** each week, according to BBC News reporting. 

The extraordinary employment arrangement exceeded the total number of hours available in a standard seven-day week, which contains only **168 hours**. According to the report, **Kashim Chowdhury** admitted to making mistakes while trying to juggle the massive portfolio of concurrent roles. 

## Accountability and Institutional Oversight

The revelations regarding the unsustainable weekly hour commitments have triggered intense scrutiny over how public sector hiring practices and monitoring systems allowed such overlapping contracts to occur unchecked. BBC News stated that the situation brought significant attention to internal controls within government agencies, raising questions about whether oversight bodies can effectively prevent individuals from accumulating impossible scheduling demands. While public administration frameworks usually mandate strict working time regulations to ensure performance quality and worker wellbeing, this case highlights glaring vulnerabilities in multi-post tracking. These administrative gaps often compound existing administrative strains, such as those seen when [bereaved civil service families face unjust tax bills](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/bereaved-civil-service-families-could-face-unjust-tax-bills-due-to-pension) due to institutional delays.

## Background Context

Public sector employment contracts are typically governed by strict working hour directives designed to limit weekly shifts and prevent burnout. However, decentralized hiring across different departments or agencies can sometimes create blind spots where independent payroll systems fail to cross-reference a candidate's existing government workload. 

## Why This Matters

This disclosure exposes systemic weaknesses in administrative oversight that directly affect public trust and the efficient allocation of taxpayer funds. When public servants accumulate workloads physically impossible to fulfill, the quality of governance deteriorates, and essential public services suffer from compromised attention. Furthermore, such incidents fuel public cynicism regarding public sector accountability, particularly at a time when ordinary citizens face stringent workplace standards and economic pressures. The situation also affects morale among fellow public workers who shoulder standard, demanding workloads while managing institutional [delays affecting civil service pensions](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/bereaved-families-could-face-unjust-tax-bill-after-civil-service-pension-delays). 

## What to Watch

Observers will monitor upcoming parliamentary inquiries and internal departmental audits to see if stricter cross-departmental vetting processes are introduced. Future developments are likely to focus on whether disciplinary measures will be enforced against the official or if management personnel responsible for approving the contracts will face administrative penalties.

Sources: [BBC News](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmze4w63ly42o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

articles.title: Why has Lord's dug up its pitch and what comes next?

articles.content: After years of comment, Lord's has dug up one of its pitches for the first time in more than 25 years. Why the drastic action and what next?
articles.aiArticle:
For the first time in over **25 years**, ground staff at the historic London cricket venue Lord's have taken the drastic step of digging up one of their pitches, following years of ongoing commentary and criticism regarding the playing surface. According to **BBC Sport**, the rare excavation marks a significant moment of maintenance for the famous ground, prompting questions about why the radical measure was taken and what procedures will follow. 

## Behind the Decision to Excavate

The drastic action comes after a prolonged period of scrutiny surrounding the behavior of the wicket, with observers and participants frequently debating its quality. While cricket venues routinely perform seasonal repairs and relay individual strips, completely digging up a pitch at this storied ground is an unusual occurrence that has not been witnessed in a quarter of a century. The report states that the ground's curators finally elected to intervene directly after years of debate accumulated around the pitch's performance. Similar to how elite sports organizations must constantly evaluate their infrastructure—much like major sports broadcasters facing questions about their long-term futures, as seen in our analysis of [Troy Aikman and Joe Buck: what next for the NFL’s $165m TV power couple as they head for a split?](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/troy-aikman-and-joe-buck-what-next-for-the-nfl-s-m)—venues must occasionally perform fundamental overhauls to stay competitive.

## Why Surface Quality Matters

> **Context:** Lord's is widely regarded as the home of cricket, meaning the condition of its playing surfaces carries immense prestige and directly impacts international Test matches, county fixtures, and player safety. When a pitch draws persistent criticism over multiple seasons, venue operators face mounting pressure to protect the ground's reputation and ensure fair competition between bat and ball. 

## The Road Ahead for the Historic Strip

What happens next remains a subject of close observation for groundskeepers, players, and administrators alike as the rebuilding process gets underway. According to **BBC Sport**, the immediate focus will center on preparing the foundation and laying new turf to ensure the strip settles properly ahead of upcoming domestic and international fixtures. Observers will be watching to see how the newly reconstructed surface behaves once competitive cricket returns to the venue, and whether the extensive labor successfully addresses the longstanding concerns that led to the rare intervention. articles.title: As fans reject AI-generated music, even boosters are drawing the line
articles.summary: Enthusiasts like Grimes and A$AP Rocky may embrace AI-generated content, but they won’t produce it themselves Streaming services, notable musicians and fans are confronting the growing presence of AI-generated music and drawing lines in the sand. On Tuesday,…
articles.content: Enthusiasts like Grimes and A$AP Rocky may embrace AI-generated content, but they won’t produce it themselves Streaming services, notable musicians and fans are confronting the growing presence of AI-generated music and drawing lines in the sand. On Tuesday, Spotify announced it had removed some 50m songs considered AI slop from its recommendations to users over the past year. Continue reading...
articles.aiArticle:
The music industry is facing a widespread pushback against artificial intelligence, with audiences and artists alike establishing firm boundaries as synthetic tracks flood streaming platforms. According to **Culture | The Guardian**, even prominent early enthusiasts of machine-learning tools—such as **Grimes** and **A$AP Rocky**—have shown reluctance to actually produce works entirely through automated systems, despite previously voicing support for the technology. 

This resistance arrives as digital platforms and major recording artists grapple with an escalating volume of synthetic audio. While technological innovation has transformed digital workflows across creative sectors—similar to how modern programming concepts are explored in our report on how [vibe coding is turning the music gear world upside down](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/vibe-coding-is-turning-the-music-gear-world-upside-down)—the commercial reception for automated art remains deeply divided. 

## The Divide Among Prominent Boosters

The report highlights a distinct paradox within the contemporary electronic and hip-hop scenes. While public-facing figures like **Grimes** and **A$AP Rocky** have experimented with or praised the conceptual framework of synthetic media, the practice of releasing fully machine-generated compositions has triggered a different reaction altogether. Fans are increasingly vocal in their rejection of tracks that lack human authorship, prompting creators and executives to reconsider their approach to automated production tools. 

Historically, popular music has always evolved alongside technological disruption, from the introduction of digital synthesizers and samplers in the 1980s to modern digital audio workstations. However, the current shift differs fundamentally because generative models can replicate specific human voices, artistic styles, and compositional structures without the original creator's consent or compensation. 

## Why This Matters

This unfolding friction goes beyond mere aesthetics, striking at the economic survival of working artists and the integrity of cultural heritage. When algorithms can instantly generate passable imitations of established musicians, copyright frameworks and royalty streams face unprecedented destabilization. Listeners are forced to question the authenticity of what they consume, while independent creators risk being crowded out by mass-produced, low-cost synthetic noise that exploits their prior work. 

## What to Watch

Observers should monitor forthcoming policy updates from major streaming services regarding automated content labeling and royalty distribution. As fan backlash hardens, the legal challenges surrounding voice cloning and unauthorized training data will likely accelerate in courts worldwide. 

Sources: [Culture | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/oct/21/artificial-intelligence-music-grimes-asap-rocky)

articles.summary: Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google's Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle's…
articles.content: Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google's Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle's infotainment hardware - eliminating the need for phone tethering, Bluetooth connections, or aux cables. It's the clearest sign yet that Spotify is ready to move beyond Apple CarPlay and Android, popular phone projection systems that currently dominate the way most people consume media in their cars. And with 34 percent of Spotify's monthly active users and 77 percent of Premium subscribers stre … Read the full story at The Verge.
articles.aiArticle:
Spotify is breaking away from smartphone-dependent mirroring systems with the release of its first fully native dashboard application, according to a report by The Verge. Operating directly on Google's Android Automotive platform, the standalone software debuts today in select Audi vehicles. Unlike traditional interfaces that rely on an external device running Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, this fresh integration runs entirely on the automobile's built-in computer hardware.

## Direct Integration Replaces Smartphone Mirroring

The newly released software is engineered to function independently of a driver's mobile phone, marking a major shift in how the streaming platform approaches dashboard audio. According to The Verge, the application lives natively within the vehicle's central display system, bypassing the need to tether a smartphone for interface access. This build arrives as automakers increasingly adopt Google's embedded operating system for factory dashboards, offering a more deeply integrated user experience than standard projection tools like CarPlay.

Behind the scenes, the audio giant continues to refine its broader software ecosystem, having recently [pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/spotify-pulled-million-ai-slop-and-spam-tracks-from-its-recommendations) to clean up user discovery. The company has also been diversifying its monetization models, rolling out features like [Spotify’s new podcast memberships let you pay for extra perks](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/spotify-s-new-podcast-memberships-let-you-pay-for-extra-perks) to give creators alternative revenue streams. 

## Context: The Shift Toward Factory-Installed Infotainment

Over the past decade, smartphone projection standards have dominated digital dashboards, allowing technology companies to bypass slow-moving automotive development cycles. However, major car manufacturers are increasingly reclaiming their dashboard real estate by partnering directly with tech giants to embed operating systems straight into the vehicle assembly line. This hardware-level integration allows for tighter control over climate controls, vehicle telemetry, and media playback without relying on Bluetooth or USB device pairing.

This transition matters because it shifts the balance of power in vehicle software from phone manufacturers back to auto brands and software platforms. Drivers benefit from faster loading times and deeper system integration, but tech companies face new challenges in maintaining fragmented vehicle-specific software builds. 

What to watch: Observers will be monitoring whether other luxury brands adopt the standalone software, and how quickly the company expands compatibility beyond Audi's initial model lineup.

Sources: [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/entertainment/1014261/spotify-native-car-app-audi-android-automotive-carplay)

articles.content: At 3pm BST / 4pm CEST Friday 23 Oct , Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst will be live taking questions from our readers about the riots and protests in France. Send your questions by email now to conversations@theguardian.com , or join the discussion on Friday After weeks of protests and a weekend of riots in which a town hall was set ablaze, 2,000-plus shops were looted, 2,300 people were arrested and 1,000 police injured, the repercussions for France – for its society and its economy – continue. Allegations of police brutality surfaced, and the violent protests unnerved investors, resulting in a debt sell-off , with borrowing costs rising higher than for Greece. All of this ahead of a hotly contested presidential election that’s now just six months away. The French government’s escalating financial problems were covered by the Guardian’s Europe correspondent Jon Henley who wrote: “France’s national debt, at 119% of GDP, is at its highest level since 1946 . Its budget deficit, at 5.1%, is also among the highest in the EU. There is just no money in the bank to ease the cost of living squeeze that brought 550,000 people on to the streets on Saturday.” Continue reading...

An ATM reportedly had the highest withdrawal rate in Europe in the 90s, as oil and gas wealth flowed through the city. articles.title: What an eyesore! My day at Norfolk’s frightful fridge mountain
articles.summary: This summer alone, 26 local authorities in the UK had to stop accepting fridges and freezers for recycling. Now the appliances are piling up around the country – with no proper disposal date in sight Not much is happening in the tiny Norfolk hamlet of Little…
articles.content: This summer alone, 26 local authorities in the UK had to stop accepting fridges and freezers for recycling. Now the appliances are piling up around the country – with no proper disposal date in sight Not much is happening in the tiny Norfolk hamlet of Little Hautbois on the day I visit. The pub, once popular with airmen from RAF Coltishall, stopped being a pub a long time ago, even before RAF Coltishall stopped being RAF Coltishall. It’s not Saturday, so there are no weddings at Hautbois Hall. Nor is it 19 May, so the restless, headless ghost of Thomas Boleyn isn’t driving his carriage across the bridge over the River Bure, as he is said to do on the anniversary of the execution of his daughter, Anne. Today, a lovely autumn one, all is as it should be. But half a mile down a narrow country lane is an incongruous and baffling sight: a strip of gentle hillside made up of large white rectangular blocks, piled up and sparkling in the sunshine. A glacier, you might think, if you were in Norway rather than Norfolk. (And ice is involved, as it happens.) As you get nearer, the picture becomes clearer; the blocks have coils on one face, doors and handles on the opposite one, plus the manufacturers’ names. It’s a glacier of fridges, more than 3,000 of them. Continue reading...

The vintage emporium is still a downtown staple, but a little of its spirit comes uptown this month with Cyndi Lauper: A Suitcase of Memories , a two-part auction of her fashion and personal items at the New York auction house Bonhams. On a recent Thursday morning in New York, the singer is sporting seafoam green hair and is in good spirits as she leads a private tour of the collection. articles.title: Making Marie Antoinette review – sweet Coppola home movie reveals the family business
articles.summary: Shot by Sofia’s mother Eleanor this documentary shows something of the strain of shooting a period piece, but is a far cry from the tumultuous portrait of her husband in Hearts of Darkness It is 20 years since the release of Sofia Coppola’s Marie Antoinette…
articles.content: Shot by Sofia’s mother Eleanor this documentary shows something of the strain of shooting a period piece, but is a far cry from the tumultuous portrait of her husband in Hearts of Darkness It is 20 years since the release of Sofia Coppola’s Marie Antoinette starring Kirsten Dunst; it is a supportively unjudging, unironised study of the queen’s early years before the 1789 revolution, lavishly and accurately costumed, shot on location at Versailles and based on the Antonia Fraser biography – but also subversively and amusingly using pop tracks from the 70s and 80s on the soundtrack. It got a storm of booing from French critics, reportedly annoyed at the way their history had been reduced to a music video and fashion shoot with no French actors involved. Or hardly any. In fact, for all the lack of political grit, the film was interesting and accomplished, and deservedly has a fanbase – and it is to that constituency that this making-of documentary from the director’s mother Eleanor Coppola is really addressed. It is basically a sweet family home movie on digital video which shows something of the strain and the longueurs of shooting a demanding period picture, but tactfully not seeing anything really explosive or bad-tempered. It is very far from Eleanor Coppola’s sensational behind-the-scenes film Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse about the tumultuous creation of Apocalypse Now, directed by her husband Francis Ford Coppola. articles.title: The Mystery of What Befell in the Ditch by Thure Erik Lund review – is this the greatest living Norwegian writer?
articles.summary: Translated into English at last, this portrait of a man appalled by modernity and desperate to get back to nature is brimming with Nordic weltschmerz T-O-M. The initials of Tomas Olsen Myrbråten, the narrator in Thure Erik Lund’s The Mystery of What Befell in…
articles.content: Translated into English at last, this portrait of a man appalled by modernity and desperate to get back to nature is brimming with Nordic weltschmerz T-O-M. The initials of Tomas Olsen Myrbråten, the narrator in Thure Erik Lund’s The Mystery of What Befell in the Ditch, spell out the Norwegian word for “empty”. Approaching 38, he’s already a relic. He spends his days slumped at the kitchen table or staring out of the window, convinced that the ceiling is about to fall and crush him. He sobs about the state he’s in and the state of society around him. Of one thing he’s sure: “It is no longer me who cries, but the world, the world crying, in me.” Nordic weltschmerz: you’d have to be a saint not to giggle. Lund has been described by Karl Ove Knausgård as the “greatest Norwegian contemporary writer”; this novel, originally published in 1999, is his first to be translated into English. In it, Tomas describes himself, over and over and over again, as a “life-of-the-mind individual”. Cursed as much as blessed, life-of-the mind individuals have a keen and unconsoling sense of how things are (“one is a wretched, contemptible, and unworthy being”) and how things will end for them (“in the sewers of society, at nature’s nadir, incessantly ground down into the mud and the mire so that one day, millions of years from now, they become oil, life-of-the-mind oil, at the very bottom of life itself”). Is he making fun of himself? In 2026, he seems closer to an eco-prophet. Continue reading...

articles.title: The New Stanford Prison Experiment review – surely no one believes this insulting TV show is real?
articles.summary: This rehash of the notorious study in which volunteers role-play as prisoners and guards pretends to be science. It isn’t – it’s patronising reality television Television has rerun the Stanford prison experiment before, most notably in 2002 when the BBC aired…
articles.content: This rehash of the notorious study in which volunteers role-play as prisoners and guards pretends to be science. It isn’t – it’s patronising reality television Television has rerun the Stanford prison experiment before, most notably in 2002 when the BBC aired The Experiment, which advertised itself as a more rigorous version of the stunt where volunteers role-play as prison guards and prisoners. The creator of the original 1971 experiment, Philip Zimbardo, would probably have criticised the new versions to preserve his own status, but the main point he made was valid. These people all know they’re on TV, he said. They’re playing to the cameras. Whether the participants in a behavioural study forget they’re part of a study is an eternal debate point. One of the strengths of the other notorious American people-are-awful research project, the Milgram experiment , was that it made the artifice part of the process, telling the volunteers that they’d spoil the science if they didn’t keep giving strangers electric shocks: “The experiment requires that you continue.” Without that, the stooges may never act naturally; if they know the experiment is also a TV show, they definitely won’t. Continue reading...

articles.title: Katya Adler: France divided over who to blame for riots and what to learn from them
articles.summary: In France and beyond there is widespread disagreement over what led to some of the worst unrest seen in French cities in modern history.
articles.content: In France and beyond there is widespread disagreement over what led to some of the worst unrest seen in French cities in modern history.
articles.aiArticle:
French society remains deeply fractured over the underlying causes of the severe urban violence that recently swept the country, according to **BBC News**. As authorities and citizens reflect on some of the worst civil unrest in modern French history, sharp disagreements persist regarding both fault lines and future lessons. 

## Deep Divisions Over Root Causes

According to the **BBC News** report, there is no domestic or international consensus on what triggered the explosive demonstrations. Observers and political factions find themselves sharply at odds over whether the breakdown in public order stems from systemic societal failures, policing methods, or broader cultural friction. These differing interpretations have complicated official efforts to address the grievances fueling the unrest, leaving the political establishment scrambling for a unified narrative.

As the situation evolved, the government implemented strict measures to regain control, mirroring strategies seen when [France announces nightly curfews 'for as long as necessary' in Paris and other cities](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/france-announces-nightly-curfews-for-as-long-as-necessary-in-paris-and). Law enforcement agencies faced immense pressure as [France protests escalate with riots, looting and 2,400 arrests – The Latest](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/france-protests-escalate-with-riots-looting-and-arrests-the-latest) highlighted the sheer scale of the civil disobedience. 

## External Exploitation and Political Rhetoric

Beyond France's borders, foreign actors and international politicians have sought to leverage the domestic crisis for their own political objectives. The report highlights how external figures have attempted to frame the riots through partisan lenses, pointing to migration and radical politics as primary drivers. Critics argue that these outside interventions distort complex domestic grievances into simplistic culture war talking points, inflaming tensions rather than offering constructive solutions.

For decades, France has wrestled with persistent social divides, particularly concerning integration, economic opportunity, and relations between marginalized urban neighborhoods and the state. These recurring tensions frequently boil over into street protests, testing the resilience of the nation's republican model and its approach to multiculturalism.

## Why This Matters

articles.title: On Another Planet They Can Save Me by Lieke Marsman review – an astonishing memoir of terminal illness
articles.summary: Published four months after her death, the poet’s reflections on mortality are both agonising and profoundly life-affirming There are no atheists in foxholes, goes the saying, and indeed social scientists and evolutionary biologists have argued that the…
articles.content: Published four months after her death, the poet’s reflections on mortality are both agonising and profoundly life-affirming There are no atheists in foxholes, goes the saying, and indeed social scientists and evolutionary biologists have argued that the experience of war or conflict drives religious belief; in 2019, Joseph Henrich and others surveyed almost 2,000 people in three post-conflict societies – Uganda, Sierra Leone and Tajikistan – and concluded that their experience of conflict had prompted them to participate in Christian and Muslim rituals and groups. Atheism, it seems, may be as fragile as faith. “No matter how attached you are to your own rational worldview, your rationality won’t survive long under the threat of imminent death,” writes the former Dutch poet laureate Lieke Marsman in her book On Another Planet They Can Save Me. Part scream, part song, it charts the gradual dissolution of her own rational assumptions, which govern everything from her views on God to extra­terrestrial life. It is a brilliant, playful, layered and humane plea for openness and hope in the face of her own foxhole of intolerable suffering. Continue reading...

articles.title: The humble one-celled alga that helped scientists win the Nobel prize
articles.summary: Chlamydomonas and its light-sensing protein help show how memories, feelings and behaviour form in our brains A tiny alga has helped show how memories, feelings and behaviour form in our brains, in research by three scientists awarded the Nobel prize for…
articles.content: Chlamydomonas and its light-sensing protein help show how memories, feelings and behaviour form in our brains A tiny alga has helped show how memories, feelings and behaviour form in our brains, in research by three scientists awarded the Nobel prize for physiology or medicine this month. Chlamydomonas is a one-celled alga that swims towards light using a light-sensing protein called channelrhodopsin, remarkably similar to the rhodopsin in our eyes. When the channelrhodopsin detects light, electrically charged ions rush into the cell from outside, triggering an electrical signal incredibly fast that tells the alga to move with its hair-like motor. articles.title: A student protest movement has gripped Serbia for two years. This weekend it will try to take power
articles.summary: Unorthodox campaign is challenging the ruling party’s 12-year reign with a bold democratic experiment On a cool autumn evening, a team of Serbian student volunteers went canvassing in the housing estates of Krnjača, a Belgrade suburb. They were equipped with…
articles.content: Unorthodox campaign is challenging the ruling party’s 12-year reign with a bold democratic experiment On a cool autumn evening, a team of Serbian student volunteers went canvassing in the housing estates of Krnjača, a Belgrade suburb. They were equipped with lanyards emblazoned with the word “victory”, a stock list of questions and a mobile app that mapped visited homes and the level of support in each. The volunteers were part of a mass student movement, Student List, that has rocked Serbia with two years of constant protests. On Sunday, the group will represent the most serious challenge Aleksandar Vučić has faced in his 12 increasingly authoritarian years in power, by putting forward their own candidates in parliamentary elections. Continue reading...

articles.title: Veggie Thursdays and vegan surprises! How Ghent became a plant-based paradise
articles.summary: In 2014, 13% of the population of this Belgian city described themselves as flexitarian. This year, 83% did. Here is how everyone was convinced to eat their greens – and love them Sixty bowls of slime-green soup sit waiting for the children to arrive. Pupils…
articles.content: In 2014, 13% of the population of this Belgian city described themselves as flexitarian. This year, 83% did. Here is how everyone was convinced to eat their greens – and love them Sixty bowls of slime-green soup sit waiting for the children to arrive. Pupils rush in from their morning lessons, grab the bowls by the handles and start slurping. No complaints, no refusals. (OK, maybe a few “bleurgh” faces.) Chicory soup dispatched, they get stuck into the main course: falafel, Mediterranean vegetable tagine and couscous. Some ask for seconds; most grab a piece of fruit for dessert and run out to play. This is a typical Thursday lunchtime in BS De Stadspoort primary school in Ghent, Belgium. Similar meat-free menus are being eaten in other schools and nurseries across the city, plus community centres, care homes and assisted living facilities, not to mention many work canteens and restaurants. Thursday in Ghent is officially “Veggie Day” , with residents encouraged to eschew any meat or fish. So how did a city get its children – and everyone else – to eat their greens? Continue reading...
